To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic kidney disease in the rat induced by puromycin aaminonucleoside is associated with reduced renal argininosuccinatesynthetase/lyase activity and reduced cationic amino-acid transporter activity in renal cortex and aorta.
chronic kidney disease (in this case, induced in rats by puromycin aminaonucleoside) is associated with a reduction in L-arginine and an increase in asymmetric dimethylarginin (ADMA).
chronic kidney disease is associated with decreased renal synthesis of L-arginine and reduced clearance of the endogenous NOS antagonist, asymmetric dimethyl-arginine (AD-MA).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of the development of hypertension in chronic kidney disease.
the role of the amino acid arginine (Arg) in cardiovascular disease (CVD) and in particular in hypertension (HTN).
the role of arginine and its metabolites in the pathophysiology of hypertension and renal disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kidney and liver are important sources of L-Arg in PAN CKD, and the kidney and aorta are important sources of ADMA.
PAN-induced CKD is associated with reduced L-Arg synthesis, uptake and utilization and increased ADMA, all contributing to reduced renal NO production.
PAN induced a progressive loss of L-Arg and its metabolites, which may have contributed to renal damage, hypertension and oxidative stress in PAN-CKD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of L-Arg availability and increased plasma ADMA contribute to the development and progression of PAN-CKD and hypertension.
reduced renal L-Arg production, increased ADMA, reduced DDAH activity and oxidative stress may contribute to PAN-CKD.
the kidney is not a major source of plasma L-Arg in PAN CKD and that the kidney is an important site of ADMA production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PAN-induced kidney damage is associated with reduced renal L-Arg and DDAH activities.
there is a complex interplay of factors that contribute to the development of hypertension and renal dysfunction in PAN-CKD.
renal and hepatic DDAHA is critical to maintain renal function and prevent hypertension in PAN-induced CKD.
